solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Top comedic actor's books sold in large numbers

parts.note: top as an adjective means best, as in the top student
Peter Sellers was the British comic actor of The Pink Panther films and The Goon Show

explanation.surface: A leading comic performer's memoirs fly off the shelves.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'actor' stands for 'has', a link joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Titles that shift huge numbers of copies are the chart-topping volumes in any bookshop's list.

clue.text: Take a swim in city close to seaside

parts.note: Bath is a city in Somerset, England, famed for its Roman spa

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Swimming in a town near the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to' looks like 'near' but means the last letter of 'seaside'.
explanation.definitionFit: To bathe in British usage means to go swimming in the sea or a lake.

clue.text: Tourist showing sense — wise man

parts.note: sight is one of the five senses
a seer is a sage or prophet

explanation.surface: A visitor showing good judgement, like a sage.
explanation.definitionFit: A visitor going round famous places to look at them is a holidaymaker or traveller.

clue.text: Ridicule side's leader, a bore

indicators.note: a word's leader is its first letter

parts.note: to tire is to weary or bore someone

explanation.surface: Mocking a team captain as a tedious person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bore' looks like a noun but is the verb TIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Mockery using irony or exaggeration to expose folly is satire.

clue.text: Cheek, and other facial feature

definitions.meaning: cheek here means impudent talk or backchat
a part of the mouth on the face

explanation.surface: Listing parts of the face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheek' looks like part of the face, but its sense here is insolence.
explanation.definitionFit: Lip is slang for impertinent talk, and also names part of the mouth.

clue.text: Rental stupidly parked across hotel entrance

indicators.note: parked across means placed on either side of something, so the jumble surrounds the hotel letter
stupidly suggests something done wrongly, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A hire car left foolishly blocking the doorway of a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrance' reads as a doorway but is the verb, accented on its second syllable: to captivate.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance someone is to captivate or spellbind them completely.

clue.text: Morsel, pretty poor for an oceanic bird

indicators.note: poor suggests the words are badly put together, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rather meagre scrap of food is offered to a seabird.
explanation.definitionFit: This small dark petrel lives far out at sea, coming ashore only to breed.

clue.text: Without warning, released article about old female, depressed

parts.note: someone released from prison is out
the is the definite article
feeling blue means feeling low or depressed

explanation.surface: A paroled prisoner unexpectedly writes about an elderly woman who is miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' here just means concerning; the article is placed after O and F.
explanation.definitionFit: Something arriving unexpectedly, like a bolt from a clear sky, comes suddenly.

clue.text: Out of bed, drunk is nervy

parts.note: someone out of bed is up for the day
tight is an informal word for drunk

explanation.surface: Someone up and already drinking is jittery.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a person tense and anxious, unable to relax.

clue.text: A pot I ordered for courtyard

indicators.note: ordered here means arranged into a new sequence, so the letters of the words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone buys a plant pot to decorate a paved yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like 'purchased' but signals the anagram of A POT I.
explanation.definitionFit: A paved outdoor area beside a house is like a small enclosed yard.

clue.text: Reverses through, then goes

parts.note: over can mean finished or through, as in 'the game is over'
a go in a game is a turn, so goes are turns

explanation.surface: A driver backs up through a junction and moves off.
explanation.definitionFit: A court that overturns a ruling reverses it, setting it aside.

clue.text: Hangs out with dreadful liar in imaginary paradise

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged
dreadful suggests something badly made, so the letters of the word after it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone spends time with a terrible fibber in a dream world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hangs out' reads as one phrase meaning socialises, but 'out' is an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Himalayan utopia of James Hilton's novel Lost Horizon became a byword for an idyllic place.

clue.text: Stuff farm animal

definitions.meaning: to stuff is to cram or force something in
a male sheep kept on a farm

explanation.surface: A farmer feeding up a beast.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramming means cramming in by force, and a tup is a male sheep found on farms.

clue.text: Mark sailor has to achieve

parts.note: tar is an old informal word for a seaman
to get a result is to achieve it

explanation.surface: A seaman named Mark must succeed in his task.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a man's name but is the definition: something aimed at.
explanation.definitionFit: A mark is something aimed at, like the bullseye a marksman shoots for.

clue.text: Plant with edible stalks? Nonsense

definitions.meaning: a garden plant whose pink stems are cooked as a dessert
meaningless talk, from the word actors mutter for background chatter

explanation.surface: A garden vegetable dismissed as rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: The crop is grown for its tart stems, and the word is also slang for drivel.

clue.text: Operation on cheek for career

indicators.note: in an across clue 'on' places the word before it after the following one

parts.note: gall means impudence or cheek

explanation.surface: Someone has surgery on the side of the face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'career' is the verb: to rush along at speed, not a job.
explanation.definitionFit: To career is to rush headlong, as a horse does at its fastest pace.

clue.text: Get here, a soft fruit

parts.note: P is piano, the musical marking for soft
a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: An invitation to arrive with a gentle piece of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: To show up or arrive somewhere is to come into view.

clue.text: Bird frequenting quagmire, mudlark

indicators.note: frequenting means being found in a place, so the bird lurks inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A large bird is spotted in a swamp alongside a scavenger of riverside mud.
explanation.definitionFit: The large flightless Australian runner is a type of bird.

clue.text: Disgusting ruling involving opener for Peterborough United

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the ruling word holds the other pieces

parts.note: regnant means reigning or ruling

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter

parts.note: U is the usual abbreviation for United in football club names

explanation.surface: A sickening refereeing decision involving the first goal for Peterborough United.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruling' looks like a noun (a decision) but is the adjective REGNANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something repulsive arouses deep distaste, the same reaction as revolting or disgusting.

clue.text: Pay for part of that on expenses

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone must reimburse a sum charged to the company account.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay for a wrong is to make amends or expiate it.

clue.text: Understand king needing knight's backing

indicators.note: backing means standing behind in support, so the knight comes after the king

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's king
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A monarch can only grasp things with a loyal knight supporting him.
explanation.definitionFit: To come to know or grasp something is to master it by study.

clue.text: Recently discovered tailless amphibian

indicators.note: tailless means the creature loses its final letter

parts.note: a newt is a small amphibian

explanation.surface: A newly found species of amphibian without a tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Something only just found or brought to light is fresh and novel.

clue.text: One in record book, typical example

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the pieces that follow

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record
a tome is a large book
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An entry in a record book shows a classic case.
explanation.definitionFit: The perfect embodiment of a type is its quintessence, a model specimen.

clue.text: Vigorous rubbing of joint with oil

parts.note: the elbow is the joint of the arm
grease is a thick oil or lubricant

explanation.surface: A massage of a sore joint using lotion.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means hard physical effort, especially in scrubbing and polishing.
